notes: Field descriptions are inferred from the shipping ETL logic, the alias definitions in the SQL, and the matching notes under Documentation/Schema/Data_Models/Customer_Order/Shipping.

fields.description: Customer account identifier from the customer order header used to group shipment activity by customer.
Customer order identifier from the sales order header.
Line number on the customer order used to distinguish multiple items on the same order.
Date the customer order was placed, derived from CUSTOMER_ORDER.ORDER_DATE.
Date the customer order record was created, derived from CUSTOMER_ORDER.CREATE_DATE.
Requested ship date for the order line, using the line-level value when available and falling back to the order header value.
Business-rule branch used to decide which date should drive the shipment filter logic for the line.
Effective date used in the shipment filter, chosen from invoice/shipment dates and desired ship dates based on the FILTER_CASE logic.
Status code from CUSTOMER_ORDER, such as active, cancelled, or held states.
Flag that indicates the line was updated or classified from a misc-reference charge description rather than a standard part record.
Service charge identifier or charge text extracted from the order line when a charge entry is embedded in MISC_REFERENCE.
Classification of the line as a service charge, part processing, or other line type.
Resolved item reference for the line, either a service charge ID or the matching part identifier.
Charge description details extracted from the misc-reference field for service-charge lines.
Customer-facing description retained when the line is driven by a misc-reference service charge or charge update.
Original part identifier on the customer order line before any fallback or correction logic.
Alternate part identifier matched from the misc-reference field when the line was recorded without a normal PART_ID.
Final part identifier used for the shipment row, with a fallback to the misc-reference match when necessary.
Part description from the PART dimension used in the shipment feed.
Product code associated with the key part.
Commodity code associated with the key part.
Planner owner assigned to the part, used in business-stream logic.
Buyer owner assigned to the part, used in business-stream and reasoning logic.
Derived numeric category that drives the adjusted due-date calculation and downstream business stream logic.
Customer-order line status flag indicating whether the line is marked as a short-shipment condition.
Original ordered quantity on the customer order line.
Total quantity shipped against the order line.
Remaining quantity before applying cancellation or overship adjustments.
Net quantity remaining to be shipped after accounting for canceled, over-shipped, and closed lines.
Unit price on the customer order line used for amount calculations.
Business stream classification for the line, such as CMP-FIN, CMP-MFG, or UNKNOWN based on planner and buyer rules.
User-defined material type pulled from the part metadata.
Packlist document identifier associated with the shipment line.
Line number on the packlist for the shipment detail.
Quantity actually shipped for the packlist line, excluding manual or special-case invoice entries.
Actual shipment date taken from the SHIPPER record.
Date on the related receivable invoice record.
Receivable invoice identifier associated with the shipment line.
Line number within the invoice record.
Amount for the invoiced line.
Quantity on the invoice line, adjusted to exclude special manual invoice cases.
Calculated shipped value equal to SHIPPED_QTY multiplied by UNIT_PRICE.
Calculated remaining value equal to UNSHIPPEDQTY multiplied by UNIT_PRICE.
Desired ship date adjusted by the REASONING day offset to support due-date and delivery analysis.
Supply linkage type from DEMAND_SUPPLY_LINK, classified as CP or WO.
Work-order base identifier for the linked supply record when the line is tied to a work order.
Work-order lot identifier from the linked supply record.
Work-order split identifier from the linked supply record.
Work-order subidentifier from the linked supply record.
Final status for the shipment line, categorized as COMPLETED, INCOMPLETE, CANCELLED, or ON HOLD??? based on shipped quantities and order conditions.
